description: Generalize the CAM-260 in-story ratchet-raise pattern from file-size to the full check:all quality spine (coverage/debt/dead-code/dup), with the worker running check:all in-story and the reviewer backstopping every loosening.

userStories.title: Implementer runs full check:all in-story with a per-gate resolution rubric
userStories.description: As the autonomous worker, I need to run the full `bun run check:all` spine in-story after coding (not just typecheck+test+file-size) and resolve each sibling ratchet (coverage, debt-markers, dead-code, dup) inline per a per-gate rubric, so a legitimate change that trips a ratchet is caught and justified during the story run rather than surfacing late at ship/CI as a manual raise.
acceptanceCriteria: subagent-implementer.md (both .claude/agents/ and templates/agents/ copies) replaces the CAM-260 file-size-only scoped exception (currently ~line 100/97, the sentence 'This is a scoped exception ... NOT a switch to running the full bun run check:all in-story') with an instruction that the worker runs the full `bun run check:all` spine in-story after coding, so coverage/debt-markers/dead-code/dup fire during the story run. [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'grep -q "full .bun run check:all. spine in-story" .claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md && grep -q "full .bun run check:all. spine in-story" templates/agents/subagent-implementer.md']

The stale scoped-exception wording is gone from both implementer copies (no remaining sentence asserting file-size is a scoped exception and NOT a switch to running the full check:all). [oracle: file-assert bash -c '! grep -q "NOT a switch to running the full" .claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md && ! grep -q "NOT a switch to running the full" templates/agents/subagent-implementer.md']

Both implementer copies document the per-gate inline-resolution rubric: coverage = lower the global floor in scripts/coverage-budget.json with a CAM tracker-ref in the top-level _ref in the same staged commit; debt-markers = cite the TODO/FIXME with an inline tracker ref on the same line; dead-code (knip) = remove the dead code OR add a justified ignore/exclude entry to knip.json; dup (jscpd) = deduplicate OR bump threshold/ignore in .jscpd.json with justification. [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'for f in .claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md templates/agents/subagent-implementer.md; do grep -q "coverage-budget.json" $f && grep -q "knip.json" $f && grep -q ".jscpd.json" $f || exit 1; done']

The rubric preserves the CAM-260 file-size raise mechanics (raise only ceilings of files this story grew, _ref staged in the same commit) and notes that coverage carries the _ref/tracker channel (two global floors: functions, lines) while knip and jscpd have NO _ref channel (their suppressions rely on the reviewer backstop, not a staged tracker-ref). [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'grep -qi "no _ref\|no .ref. channel\|reviewer backstop" .claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md']

An ADR under docs/adr/ documents the reversal of the CAM-260 scoping decision (worker now runs full check:all in-story), records the trade-off (slower per-story loop vs early-catch of the whole ratchet class) and the rejected alternatives (coverage-only; per-unit budget files + _ref gates for knip/jscpd). [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'grep -qi "reverses CAM-260\|reverses cam-260" docs/adr/0023-implementer-runs-full-check-all-in-story-reverses-cam-260-scoped-gate-decision.md && grep -qi "rejected" docs/adr/0023-implementer-runs-full-check-all-in-story-reverses-cam-260-scoped-gate-decision.md']
The embedded copy is regenerated via `bun run embed-vendor` and the drift check is clean. [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check). [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]

GOTCHA: the two copies are NOT byte-identical by design (.claude/ is cam-specific, templates/ is generic) - preserve each file's existing register, do not force them byte-identical. Editing templates/agents/ REQUIRES `bun run embed-vendor` to regenerate src/vendor/_generated.ts or the byte-parity test (test/embedded.test.ts) fails and the plan preflight aborts (the exact CAM-260 preflight-abort failure mode). Gate wiring reference: scripts/check-all.ts GATES manifest (coverage=check-coverage.ts over scripts/coverage-budget.json floors; dead-code=knip@6.24.0 with knip.json ignore/exclude; dup=jscpd@5 with .jscpd.json threshold/ignore). Config files this story does NOT modify (they are referenced by the rubric only): scripts/coverage-budget.json, knip.json, .jscpd.json, scripts/check-coverage.ts. coverage has FLOOR_TOLERANCE_PP=0.5 slack (a floor lower within tolerance is not a real regression). The current implementer scoped-exception text is at .claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md line ~100 (step 2 of 'What you do for the story'). ADR 0023 already exists (written at spec time by the domain-docs step, commit cb8427b1); verify its content matches the reversal decision rather than recreating it. This story touches .claude/agents/** which the implementer normally must not touch - it is explicitly required here. Re-check docs/adr/0023 and docs/adr/0022 before editing.

userStories.title: Reviewer backstops raises/suppressions across all four sibling ratchets
userStories.description: As the reviewer, I need my file-size-budget backstop extended to cover coverage-floor lowering, dead-code (knip) suppressions, and dup (jscpd) loosenings, so that for each of the four sibling gates I confirm the change was legitimate rather than the gate being loosened to pass - the only guard for knip/jscpd, which have no staged tracker-ref channel.
acceptanceCriteria: subagent-reviewer.md (both .claude/agents/ and templates/agents/ copies) extends the existing file-size-budget backstop (currently the checklist item at ~line 86) so the reviewer explicitly backstops loosenings across all four sibling gates: a coverage-floor lowering in scripts/coverage-budget.json, a dead-code suppression (knip.json ignore/exclude), and a dup loosening (.jscpd.json threshold/ignore), in addition to file-size ceiling raises. [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'for f in .claude/agents/subagent-reviewer.md templates/agents/subagent-reviewer.md; do grep -q "coverage-budget.json" $f && grep -q "knip.json" $f && grep -q ".jscpd.json" $f || exit 1; done']

The reviewer instruction states that for coverage a staged _ref tracker-ref can be checked, but knip and jscpd have NO _ref channel, so the reviewer backstop is the only guard for those two loosenings (do not require a fabricated _ref for them). [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'grep -qi "only guard\|no _ref\|no .ref. channel" .claude/agents/subagent-reviewer.md']

The project-conventions row (criterion #5 in the Layer B rubric table, ~line 116) references that every raise/suppression across the four sibling gates in the diff is justified, extending the existing file-size-budget clause. [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'grep -qi "coverage\|knip\|jscpd\|sibling" .claude/agents/subagent-reviewer.md | head -1 >/dev/null && grep -n "project-conventions" .claude/agents/subagent-reviewer.md']

An unjustified raise/suppression on any of the four gates is documented as a CRITICAL / REQUEST CHANGES finding (same disposition as the existing file-size clause). [oracle: file-assert bash -c 'grep -qi "REQUEST CHANGES\|CRITICAL" .claude/agents/subagent-reviewer.md']
The embedded copy is regenerated via `bun run embed-vendor` and the drift check is clean. [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check). [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
The full quality spine is green. [oracle: bun run check:all]
